title: Utility Services Terms: One Utility Account per Apartment Home and Lease
content:
# One Utility Account per Apartment Home — Utility Services Program

**Clause 1.** Each apartment home under a lease has exactly one utility account of the Utility Services Program, so a household normally holds one. During an in-community transfer the account of the apartment home left behind stays in final billing while the account of the new apartment home opens, which is why two accounts may be open at once; a household holds at most 2 utility accounts at one time.

**Clause 2.** A new utility account may be opened only when no other pending or active utility account exists for the same lease. An account in final billing does not block the new one.

## Basis of the condition in Clause 2

- The condition is read from the system's records of the utility accounts, before the new account is opened — not from the customer's account of events.
- The comparison is made on the same lease: the accounts that count are those recorded for the lease the new account would serve.
- Only accounts in pending or active status stand in the way.

## Status of an existing account on the same lease

| Existing account's status | Effect on opening a new account for that lease |
|---|---|
| pending | a new account may not be opened |
| active | a new account may not be opened |
| final billing | does not block the new account |

*Example (hypothetical transfer):* a household moves from one apartment home to another within the same community. The account of the home left behind has entered final billing on the transfer move date; it does not block the account of the new apartment home. For that period the household has 2 accounts open — the one in final billing and the new one.
